allowlist.reason: Stricter than valid_datetime: requires exactly six fractional digits, because acknowledgement cursors are written from to_char(...US) timestamps. Passed to decode_record_cursor as its timestamp check.
Not Lua parsing: the pattern sits inside a SQL substring(... from '^at://...') that extracts the DID authority in the database. The inline rule cannot tell SQL text from Lua code.
Takes a nullable flag: sidecars (contributors) omit indexedAt when missing while the top-level activity emits JSON null, which one record_view or record_view_omitting_indexed_at cannot express.

Position cursor {v,u,i} with no direction or timestamp and its own error message ("belongs to another collection"). It already shares the hex prologue through decode_hex_cursor_token; only the shape check is local.
Not a query parser: it checks that an indexed evaluation record field is a list. The name only resembles the repeated-parameter parsers.
Adds prefix columns and strict validation of the row on top of record_view, which it already calls; the wrapper is the endpoint-specific part.
The cursor carries the caller-supplied before datetime (no length bound); the shared 8192-character cap could reject a cursor the API issued.
The cursor carries the caller-supplied before datetime (no length bound), so the shared 8192-character cap could reject a cursor the API itself issued. Also has its own shape {v,t,u,b} and messages.
Wraps the JSON decode in pcall so a corrupt indexed record raises RecentFollowsQueryFailed instead of a generic error; record_view has no such error contract.
Declined change: the cursor must be a string (a number is rejected) with the message "cursor must occur once as a string", while the shared scalar() accepts numbers and says "cursor must occur once".
The cursor carries the author filter (f), so its size is not bounded by an AT-URI; the shared 8192-character cap could reject a cursor the API issued.
